least possible deviations from that ‘regression line.’ From the coordinates, it tries to 
formulate a linear equation that describes that ‘best-fit’ line:

Linear regression
R2 or R-squared indicates the amount of variation in a regression model
When you add a predictor to the model, R2 should increase (more variation 
explained) or remain as is (the new factor does not explain much extra)
R2
adj or Adjusted R-squared tells you the variation for a multiple regression 
model, pointing out goodness of fit (how well your sample represents the actual 
population data)
Error

Sum of Squared Residuals (SSR)
Sum of Squared estimate of Errors (SSE)
Deviation of the model from the empirical data
Small error means tightly fitting data

Not every value falls exactly on the 
regression line. There will always be 
some difference left. We call that:
Error
Standard deviation
Variance
Residue
Tension
The loss function
Deviations may lie above the line, other below. We get rid of negative values by squaring 
the error and then calculate their sum: the sum of squared error (SSE) or of residual 
(SSR), telling the difference between the observed values and the predicted values. In 
NNs, they call it the ‘loss function’ between input and expected output
That’s why we write:
y = a1x1 + a2x2 + … + anxn + b + error
Much of the literature in ML and 
Deep Learning is about reducing 
the loss function

pages.text:
Logistic regression (actually: Logistic classification)
In linear regression, the logistic function is a kind of sigmoid (S-curve), typically used for 
data classification (this is a fish, that is a hat)
f(x) = 1 / 1 + e-x
Linear regression uses the full range of continuous data
Logistic regression (classification) cuts the data into two: in or out, yes or no, 1 or 0, and 
tries to predict the category with a certain probability value
That makes life easier but mind you, regression told us life is more complex than a simple 
binary classification: in or out (e.g., some hats are modeled after fish)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logistic_function
The Euler number e is a constant of about 
2.72 and the base of natural logarithms 
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E_(mathematical_constant)

pages.text:
Used for complex relationships among variables, combining aspects of factor analysis and multiple 
regression (Jöreskog & Sörbom, 1984). Analyses both direct and indirect relationships between 
observed and latent variables. Note: you need a huge sample to run SEM (else, go to PROCESS)
Observed Variables: variables that can be directly measured or observed in the study, also referred 
to as manifest variables
Latent Variables: variables not directly observed but inferred from observed variables. They 
represent underlying constructs or factors
Measurement Model: this part of SEM specifies how latent variables are measured by the 
observed variables. It is essentially a confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) that defines the 
relationships between latent variables and their indicators. Tells whether you measured things well
Structural Model: this part specifies the relationships among latent variables. It is similar to a path 
analysis we saw previously and shows how latent variables influence one another. Tells in how far 
the data fit with your ideas
Structural Equation Modeling

pages.text:
Model Specification: define the hypothesised relationships among variables. This involves creating a 
diagram that visually represents the model, including both measurement and structural components
Model Identification: ensure that the model is mathematically identifiable, meaning there are enough data 
points to estimate the model parameters (hence, the huge sample)
Model Estimation: use statistical software to estimate the parameters of the model. Common estimation 
methods include Maximum Likelihood (ML), Generalized Least Squares (GLS), and Weighted Least Squares 
(WLS)
Model Evaluation: assess the fit of the model using various fit indices. Common fit indices include the Chi-
Square Test, Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA), Comparative Fit Index (CFI), and Tucker-
Lewis Index (TLI)
Model Modification: if the initial model does not fit well, make modifications based on theoretical 
considerations and modification indices provided by the software
Model Interpretation: interpret the estimated parameters to understand the relationships among 
variables. This includes examining direct, indirect, and total effects
Structural Equation Modeling: Steps to take
34/51

ummary
Correlation and regression gauge the relationship 
between two or more variables. Correlation measures 
the strength of a linear relationship between two 
variables. Regressions estimate how two or more 
variables have an effect on each other (i.e., regression is 
inferential)
With more predictors (independent variables), you use 
Multiple linear regression. Those independents can either 
be continuous or nominal (i.e., qualitative data). Yet, the 
dependent variable is measured on a continuous scale
Regression can be used for Neural Networks to model the 
relationship between a dependent variable and one or 
more independents. However, Neural Networks have 
more layers of regression so that ‘learning’ (= updating 
weights) can take place of more complex relationships 
between inputs and outputs

pages.text_norm: ummary Correlation and regression gauge the relationship between two or more variables. Correlation measures the strength of a linear relationship between two variables. Regressions estimate how two or more variables have an effect on each other (i.e., regression is inferential) With more predictors (independent variables), you use Multiple linear regression. Those independents can either be continuous or nominal (i.e., qualitative data). Yet, the dependent variable is measured on a continuous scale Regression can be used for Neural Networks to model the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independents. However, Neural Networks have more layers of regression so that ‘learning’ (= updating weights) can take place of more complex relationships between inputs and outputs Socrates 44/51

regression tries to predict whether an item is in-class or 
out. It is a crude measure that cuts away all intermediate 
values, reducing interval measurement to nominal scale. 
Some older Neural Networks make use of logistic 
regression
Mediation-moderation analysis provides a nuanced 
understanding of the relationships between variables, 
helping researchers and practitioners identify not just 
whether an effect exists, but also how, why, and under 
what conditions it occurs

Mediation effect
Moderation effect

Moderated mediation

Exam Sample Item
Category “Insight“
This item is about Lecture 08: (Multiple) regression. A correlation is not causation but how about linear 
regression? In linear regression, is the statement correct that correlation between dependent and 
independent variable comes from causation?
A
No. Arguing from correlation to cause may be reasonable under the correct conditions; 
otherwise, it is a fallacious inference
B
Yes. Changes in the dependent variable are predicted from and tested against changes
in the independent variable
C
Yes, by employing defeasible reasoning, inductive arguments can be raised based on
correlational data
D
No. Regression should account for measurement error, providing more accurate estimates
of relationships among variables

Exam Sample Item
Category “Insight“
In Lecture 08: (Multiple) regression, we discussed Structural Equation Modeling developed by Jöreskog
and Sörbom (1984). SEM can infer latent variables (e.g., êta2) as underlying constructs from the directly 
measurable questionnaire items (here, y9, …, 12). Does SEM rely on an ex-consequentia fallacy by 
inferring the cause (latent variable) from the effects (item scores)?
A
Yes. From X Y does not follow Y X
B
No. From Y X does not follow X Y
C
No. The latent variable is predicted from observables and 
then tested, allowing for a margin of unexplained variance (zêta2)
D
Yes. Because of the error in measurement (e9, …, 12), one 
cannot be sure that items y9, …, 12 come from êta2
49/51
